topics.title: Lymphoid Structures: Lymph Node, Spleen & Thymus
topics.productionRationale: The architecture topic: where immune responses happen — B-cell follicle vs T-cell paracortex (and the dendritic-cell trafficking that connects them), white vs red pulp with the PALS/marginal-zone zones, and the thymus as the T-cell school with its tumor/involution pitfalls. The drainage-association map is the classic anatomy-exam crossover.

topics.title: Innate vs Adaptive Immunity
topics.productionRationale: The first principles split: fast/germline-encoded/nonspecific vs slow/rearranged/specific with memory — with immune privilege (eye, testis, placenta, CNS) as the boundary condition the exam loves to probe.

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026

textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Five-row two-column table (COMPONENTS / MECHANISM / RESPONSE TO PATHOGENS / SECRETED PROTEINS / KEY FEATURES IN PATHOGEN RECOGNITION) contrasting innate (neutrophils... TLRs, PAMPs/DAMPs, NF-κB) with adaptive (T/B cells, V(D)J, memory, immunosenescence).

topics.title: MHC I vs MHC II and Bare Lymphocyte Syndrome
faSubsections: Major histocompatibility complex I and II
topics.productionRationale: The antigen-display machinery: MHC I (all nucleated cells, platelets; endogenous peptides, CD8) vs MHC II (professional APCs; exogenous peptides, CD4), the classic comparison table, and bare lymphocyte syndrome as the transcription-failure phenotype.

textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Seven-row two-column table (LOCI / BINDING / STRUCTURE / EXPRESSION / FUNCTION / ANTIGEN LOADING / ASSOCIATED PROTEINS) with the printed mnemonics (loci letter counts; CD8 × MHC 1 = 8; CD4 × MHC 2 = 8).

topics.title: HLA Subtypes Associated with Diseases
topics.productionRationale: The association map: B27 (ankylosing spondylitis, IBD, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis), DQ2/DQ8 (celiac), DQB1*0602 (narcolepsy), DR3/DR4 (T1DM), DR4 (RA), DR5 (Hashimoto/pernicious anemia), DRB1*15:01 (MS), B*58:01 (allopurinol hypersensitivity), DRB1*01:03 (IBD). Pure pattern-recognition currency — a table note, no custom visual needed.

topics.title: Major Functions of NK, B and T Cells
faSubsections: Major functions of natural killer cells
Major functions of B and T cells
topics.productionRationale: The effector roster: NK cells as the MHC-I-missing-self killers (kill tumor/virus cells with ↓ MHC I; activate via IL-2/IL-15/IFN; perforin/granzymes), B cells as antibody factories + APCs, T cells as the cytokine/effector arm — the cell-function table the whole chapter builds on.

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: Major functions of B and T cells — two-column function roster
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: A structured function list: 'B cells' (Humoral immunity; Recognize and present antigen—undergo somatic hypermutation to optimize antigen specificity; Produce antibody—differentiate into plasma cells to secrete specific immunoglobulins; Maintain immunologic memory—memory B cells persist and accelerate future response to antigen) beside 'T cells' (Cell-mediated immunity; CD4+ T cells help B cells make antibodies and produce cytokines to recruit phagocytes and activate other leukocytes; CD8+ T cells directly kill virus-infected and tumor cells via perforin and granzymes (similar to NK cells); Type IV hypersensitivity reaction; Acute and chronic cellular organ rejection).
textbookVisuals.kypLocation: blocks[2] — 'Major functions of B and T cells — verbatim' table block

topics.title: T-Cell Development: Thymic Selection & Subset Lineages
topics.productionRationale: The thymic school: positive selection in cortex (MHC recognition → survival), negative selection in medulla (high self-affinity → apoptosis or Treg), AIRE deficiency → autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome, then the helper lineage table (Th1/Th2/Th17/Treg cytokines and functions).

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: Differentiation of T cells — the four-column pathway diagram
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Four vertical columns (Bone marrow → Thymus → Lymph node → Peripheral blood): a T-cell precursor leaves the bone marrow, enters the thymus (an anatomical lobed illustration with Cortex and Medulla leader labels) as a double-positive CD4+ CD8+ thymocyte, passes positive selection (+ icon, cortex) and negative selection (− icon, medulla), exits as CD8+ Cytotoxic (upper path) or CD4+ Helper (lower path); the Helper cell fans into Th1 / Th2 / Th17 / Treg circles, each arrow labeled with promoting (+) and inhibiting (−) cytokines (Th1: +IFN-γ, IL-12 / −IL-4, IL-10; Th2: +IL-2, IL-4 / −IFN-γ; Th17: +TGF-β, IL-1, IL-6 / −IFN-γ, IL-4; Treg: +TGF-β, IL-2 / −IL-6), feeding the Secretes/Function table at right.

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Two-column table (Secretes / Function) with four rows: Th1 (IFN-γ, IL-2 / Activate macrophages and cytotoxic T cells), Th2 (IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-10, IL-13 / Activate eosinophils, ↑IgE), Th17 (IL-17, IL-21, IL-22 / Induce neutrophilic infiltration), Treg (TGF-β, IL-10, IL-35 / Prevent autoimmunity (maintain tolerance)).
textbookVisuals.kypLocation: blocks[1] — 'Helper subsets — Secretes / Function (verbatim)' table block

topics.title: Effector T Cells: Cytotoxic, Regulatory & the Macrophage Interface
topics.productionRationale: The CD8 kill (perforin/granzyme B apoptosis of virus-infected/neoplastic/graft cells via MHC I), the Th1-macrophage activation loop (IFN-γ + CD40L-CD40), and the Treg brake (CD3/CD4/CD25/FOXP3; IL-10/TGF-β; IPEX when FOXP3 fails).

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: Cytotoxic vs regulatory T cells — the source's two prose rosters
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Two prose function lists: 'Cytotoxic T cells' (Kill virus-infected, neoplastic, and donor graft cells by inducing apoptosis; Release cytotoxic granules containing preformed proteins (eg, perforin, granzyme B); CD8 binds to MHC I on virus-infected cells) and 'Regulatory T cells' (Help maintain specific immune tolerance by suppressing CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell effector functions; Identified by expression of CD3, CD4, CD25, and FOXP3; Activated Tregs produce anti-inflammatory cytokines (eg, IL-10, TGF-β); IPEX syndrome — FOXP3 deficiency → autoimmunity, enteropathy, endocrinopathy, nail dystrophy, dermatitis, diabetes in male infants).
textbookVisuals.kypLocation: blocks[1] — 'Cytotoxic vs regulatory T cells — verbatim' table block

topics.title: Lymphocyte Activation, Peripheral Tolerance & Anergy
topics.productionRationale: Signal 1 + signal 2 (costimulation) as the decision gate — CD28-B7 for T cells, CD40L-CD40 + cytokines for B cells — and what happens without signal 2: anergy or deletion; CTLA-4/PD-1 as the inhibitory checkpoints (and the drug targets they became).

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: T- and B-cell activation — the two two-signal diagrams
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Two side-by-side vector diagrams. Left (T-cell activation): an Antigen-presenting cell (Antigen on MHC II/I) faces a Naïve T cell (T cell receptor, CD4/8); signal 1 = antigen-MHC to TCR; signal 2 = CD80/86 (B7) on the APC to CD28 on the naïve T cell; output box 'Activated T cell actions'. Right (B-cell activation and class switching): an Activated CD4+ T cell (T cell receptor, CD4, CD40L) faces a B cell (B cell receptor, MHC II with Antigen, CD40); signal 1 = antigen-MHC II to TCR; signal 2 = CD40L to CD40; Cytokines arrow from the Th cell direct class switching; output box 'Activated B cell actions'.

topics.title: Antibody Structure & Function
topics.productionRationale: The immunoglobulin anatomy: heavy/light chains, constant (isotype/complement-FcR binding) vs variable (antigen binding) regions, hinge flexibility, Fab vs Fc, and the papain vs pepsin cleavage map — the structural foundation for every isotype and engineering question.

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: Antibody structure — the Y-shaped IgG anatomy diagram
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: A vector-drawn Y-shaped IgG: two Fab arms each with hypervariable V domains (VH, VL) at the tips (Antigen-binding site, Epitope labels) above constant domains (CH1, CL); a Hinge region with SS (disulfide) bonds; an Fc stem of heavy-chain-only CH2 and CH3 domains with Complement binding and Macrophage binding pointers; legend C = Constant, V = Variable, L = Light, H = Heavy, SS = Disulfide bond.

textbookVisuals.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
textbookVisuals.visualPurpose: Antibody function trio — neutralization / opsonization / complement activation
textbookVisuals.sourceFigureDescription: Three function illustrations with captions: Neutralization (antibody prevents bacterial adherence); Opsonization (antibody promotes phagocytosis by marking pathogens for destruction, C3b); Complement activation (antibody activates complement, enhancing opsonization and lysis — membrane attack complex [MAC]). The 467x329 cmyk raster on the page belongs to this function set.
textbookVisuals.kypLocation: bottom function-trio strip of the same registry visual

topics.title: Immunoglobulin Isotypes & Antigen Memory
topics.productionRationale: The isotype roster (IgG: placenta/complement/opsonin; IgA: secretions/dimer with J chain; IgM: pentamer/first/complement; IgD: receptor; IgE: parasites/mast-cell FcεRI) plus thymus-independent (repeated epitopes, no class switching/memory) vs thymus-dependent antigens.

topics.title: The Complement System
topics.productionRationale: The cascade: classical (IgG/IgM immune complexes, C1qrs), lectin (mannan-binding lectin), alternative (microbial surfaces, spontaneous C3 tickover) → C3 convertases → C3b opsonization → C5 convertase → MAC (C5b-9); the anaphylatoxins C3a/C4a/C5a; and the inhibitors (C1-INH, DAF/CD55, CD59) whose failure causes disease.

topics.title: Complement Disorders & Pathway Testing
topics.productionRationale: The deficiency patterns: early components (C1-C4) → immune-comcomplex disease + encapsulated bugs; terminal (C5-C9) → Neisseria; C1-INH → hereditary angioedema; DAF/CD59 loss → PNH. Plus the lab interpretation: classical pathway CH50 ↓ with immune-complex disease, alternative pathway AH50, and the combined testing logic.

topics.title: Important Cytokines
topics.productionRationale: The signaling roster: macrophage IL-1 (fever, acute phase), IL-6 (acute phase, B-cell growth), TNF-α (cachexia, endothelial activation/sepsis), IL-8 (neutrophil chemotaxis), IL-12 (NK/Th1); T-cell IL-2 (T-cell growth — and the transplant-drug target), IL-3; Th1 IFN-γ; Th2 IL-4/5/10/13 — each tied to the drug or disease that makes it exam-currency.

topics.title: Respiratory Burst & Type I Interferons
topics.productionRationale: The NADPH oxidase enzyme complex (O2 → O2⁻) with myeloperoxidase (HOCl) and catalase-positive S. aureus as the CGD signature — plus the female-carrier lupus-like discoid rash story; and type I IFN (IFN-α/β) as the innate antiviral: induces PKR/2'5'-oligoadenylate synthetase/RNase L in virus-infected cells, blocks viral spread.

topics.title: Cell Surface Proteins: The CD Marker Map
topics.productionRationale: The identification codes: CD3 (all T), CD4/CD8 (helper/cytotoxic), CD25+FOXP3 (Treg), CD19/20 (B), CD56 (NK), CD14/CD40 (macrophage), CD34 (HSC) — plus the drug targets (anti-CD3, rituximab anti-CD20) and the flow-cytometry reading skill this map enables.

topics.title: Active vs Passive Immunity & Vaccination
topics.productionRationale: Acquired immunity routes: active (recovery, live/killed/subunit/conjugate/toxoid/mRNA vaccines — with the memory/booster logic of each) vs passive (IgG placenta, breast milk IgA, antitoxin/IVIG — immediate but waning), and the conjugate-vaccine trick that gives polysaccharides a T-cell face.

topics.title: Autoantibodies and Their Disease Associations
topics.productionRationale: The serology directory: dsDNA/Sm (lupus), SS-A/SS-B (Sjögren), Scl-70/centromere (scleroderma/CREST), Jo-1 (myositis/polymyositis), anti-CCP (RA), anti-Jo1, anti-Mi-2, ANCA patterns, anti-histone (drug-induced lupus), anti-RNP (MCTD), anti-topoisomerase — organized by disease family for the two-step matching question. Table note, no custom visual needed.

topics.title: B-Cell Immunodeficiencies
topics.productionRationale: The antibody-failure family: Bruton (X-linked, BTK, no B cells, recurrent encapsulated/Giardia after 6 months), selective IgA (most common, asymptomatic/anaphylaxis to transfusion), CVID (↓ IgG/IgA, onset 20s-30s) — each mapped to the missing developmental step.

topics.title: T-Cell & Phagocyte Immunodeficiencies
topics.productionRationale: The cell-mediated failure spectrum: DiGeorge (22q11, thymic aplasia, T-cell lack), IL-12 receptor (mycobacteria), Job (STAT3, eczema/cold abscesses/candida), CMC (T-cell defect); combined — SCID (various, no T/B), ataxia-telangiectasia (ATM), hyper-IgM (CD40L, no class switching), Wiskott-Aldrich (WAS, thrombocytopenia+eczema+recurrent infections); phagocyte — LAD-1 (no rolling → no pus), Chédiak-Higashi (granule fusion), CGD (NADPH oxidase, catalase+ abscesses).

topics.title: Infections in Immunodeficiency
topics.productionRationale: The back-conversion: given the organism pattern, name the immune defect — encapsulated bacteria (B-cell/complement/splenectomy), intracellular bacteria/fungi/parasites (T-cell/phagocyte), viruses (T-cell), Giardia/Cryptosporidium/Campylobacter (IgA/B-cell), Pseudomonas/Aspergillus (neutropenia/phagocyte), Staph aureus/catalase+ (CGD), Serratia/Pseudomonas without pus (LAD).

topics.title: Transplant Rejection
topics.productionRationale: The rejection clock: hyperacute (minutes-hours, preformed anti-HLA/ABO antibodies, complement, thrombosis), acute (weeks-months, type IV cellular + type II humoral, reversible with immunosuppression), chronic (months-years, fibrosis/vascular intimal thickening, irreversible), GVHD (donor T cells vs host, GI/skin/liver — the bone-marrow and solid-organ risk profiles).

topics.title: Immunosuppressants
topics.productionRationale: The transplant pharmacology: calcineururin inhibitors (cyclosporine/tacrolimus — inhibit IL-2 transcription, nephrotoxicity), mTOR (sirolimus — blocks IL-2 receptor signaling, hyperlipidemia/cytopenias), anti-IL-2R (basiliximab), antiproliferatives (azathioprine/mycophenolate), and glucocorticoids (lymphocyte apoptosis) — each mechanism tied to its signature toxicity.

topics.title: Recombinant Cytokines & Clinical Uses
topics.productionRationale: Cytokines as drugs: EPO (renal anemia), G-CSF (neutropenia, stem-cell mobilization), thrombopoietin agonists (ITP), IL-2 (renal cell melanoma), IFN-α (HBV/HCV, hairy cell), IFN-β (MS), IFN-γ (CGD) — each tied to the immunology it came from. Compact reference note, no custom visual needed.
